section: Earthquakes - causes, seismic waves, measurement, distribution, effects

accepted.s: Etna is located in which of the following regions and is characterised by which status?
accepted.x: Etna is an active stratovolcano located in Sicily, Italy.
accepted.tq: Use the country-region and volcano-status pair together to avoid confusing Etna with other Italian volcanoes.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Mount Etna is correct?
o: It is Europe's largest and most active volcano, rises to about 3,300 m and became a UNESCO site in 2013.
It is Africa's highest peak and has been dormant since 1707.
It is the world's highest active volcano at 6,893 m.
It is an extinct volcano that buried Pompeii in AD 79.
accepted.x: Etna is Europe's largest and most active volcano, is approximately 3,300 m high and has been a UNESCO site since 2013.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related volcano facts by checking the continent, height, status and historical association.

accepted.s: The volcano associated with the burial of Pompeii in AD 79 is:
accepted.x: Mount Vesuvius is an active volcano in Italy and buried Pompeii in AD 79.
accepted.tq: Apply the famous-event association to identify the correct volcano.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ojos del Salado is in Chile and is the world's highest active volcano, at 6,893 m; it is not dormant.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched status by separating country facts from active-dormant classifications.

accepted.s: The last recorded eruption of Fujiyama mentioned in the geographical record was in:
accepted.x: Fujiyama in Japan is dormant, and its last eruption occurred in 1707.
accepted.tq: Test the precise historical year rather than relying only on the volcano's country or status.

accepted.s: Which volcano is recognised as the world's highest active volcano?
accepted.x: Ojos del Salado in Chile is the world's highest active volcano, with an elevation of 6,893 m.
accepted.tq: Use the superlative and the numerical height as the decisive clues.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Volcan de Fuego is Guatemala's most active stratovolcano.
2. Its Strombolian eruptions may occur every 15–20 minutes.
3. It erupted again in June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Volcan de Fuego is Guatemala's most active stratovolcano, has frequent Strombolian eruptions and erupted again in June 2026.
accepted.tq: Check the location, eruption frequency and recent-event details independently before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Popocatepetl, which has been active since 1994, is located in:
accepted.x: Popocatepetl is an active volcano in Mexico and has been active since 1994.
accepted.tq: Use the country-status-year combination to distinguish neighbouring Latin American volcanoes.

accepted.s: Which of the following recent volcano-related events is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Mayon is in the Philippines and is noted for its symmetrical composite-cone form. Mount Dukono is in Halmahera, Indonesia, while Mount Spurr is in Alaska's Aleutian Arc.
accepted.tq: Match each volcano with its location and distinguishing description, rejecting swapped-location traps.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a volcanic product?
accepted.x: Pyroclastic debris, volcanic bombs and lava are volcanic products. Atmospheric air is not listed as a volcanic product.
accepted.tq: Classify the physical materials emitted or produced by volcanoes and identify the outsider.

accepted.s: Which gas is present in the greatest proportion among the principal gases released by volcanoes?
accepted.x: Volcanic gases consist mostly of water vapour, followed by carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide and hydrogen sulphide.
accepted.tq: Recall the stated order of abundance rather than confusing gases with solid volcanic products.

accepted.s: A volcano that is presently quiet but may erupt in the future is classified as:
accepted.x: A dormant volcano is quiet at present but retains the possibility of erupting. An extinct volcano is not expected to erupt.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the similar status terms dormant and extinct by focusing on future eruptive possibility.

accepted.s: A volcano is considered extinct when:
o: It is quiet temporarily but may erupt
It is erupting or has erupted recently
accepted.x: An extinct volcano is one from which no eruption is expected; temporary quietness describes a dormant volcano.
accepted.tq: Compare the status definitions directly and reject the tempting reversal of dormant and extinct.

accepted.s: Which one of the following volcanoes is an example of a shield volcano?
accepted.x: Mauna Loa is a shield volcano formed by fluid basaltic lava and characterised by gentle slopes.
accepted.tq: Link the volcano example to the defining lava type and slope profile.

accepted.s: Shield volcanoes are generally characterised by:
o: Several vents and overlapping lava domes in every case
Fluid basaltic lava and gentle slopes
A large depression formed only by erosion
Thick viscous lava, steep cones and explosive eruptions
accepted.x: Shield volcanoes have fluid basaltic lava and gentle slopes. Thick viscous lava and explosive steep cones are characteristic of composite volcanoes.
accepted.tq: Use the contrast between lava viscosity and slope to distinguish shield and composite volcanoes.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about composite or stratovolcanoes:
1. They generally have thick and viscous lava.
2. They commonly form steep cones.
3. They are associated with explosive eruptions.
4. They constitute approximately 60% of the Earth's volcanoes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Composite or stratovolcanoes have viscous lava, steep cones, explosive activity and constitute approximately 60% of Earth's volcanoes.
accepted.tq: Test a group of defining characteristics together, including the quantitative share.

accepted.s: A large depression formed by the collapse of a volcano after an explosive eruption is called a:
accepted.x: A caldera is a large depression produced by collapse following an explosive eruption.
accepted.tq: Identify the landform from its formation process rather than from an example alone.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mauna Loa — caldera formed by explosive collapse
Mount Aso — one of the world's largest calderas
Etna — complex volcano with several overlapping vents only
Dukono — shield volcano with gentle basaltic slopes
accepted.x: Mount Aso is one of the world's largest calderas. Mauna Loa is a shield volcano, while Dukono is listed as a complex volcano.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive example of a landform and then eliminate type-example reversals.

accepted.s: Complex or compound volcanoes are distinguished by the presence of:
o: Several vents, overlapping cones and lava domes
Only fluid basaltic lava and very gentle slopes
A single crater with no secondary vents
No lava and no eruptive products
accepted.x: Complex or compound volcanoes contain several vents, overlapping cones and lava domes. Taal and Dukono are examples.
accepted.tq: Recall the structural features of the volcano type before considering its examples.

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a complex or compound volcano?
accepted.x: Taal in the Philippines is a complex or compound volcano. Dukono is in Indonesia, while Mount Aso is a caldera in Japan.
accepted.tq: Use the sure example-location pair and reject nearby country substitutions.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Strombolian and Vulcanian eruptions?
o: Vulcanian eruptions consist only of gentle lava flows.
Strombolian eruptions are frequent and mild, whereas Vulcanian eruptions are more explosive.
Strombolian eruptions are always more explosive than Vulcanian eruptions.
Both terms refer exclusively to dormant volcanoes.
accepted.x: Strombolian eruptions involve frequent, mild bursts of bombs and ash, whereas Vulcanian eruptions are more explosive.
accepted.tq: Compare the intensity and nature of the two similarly named eruption styles.

accepted.s: A seismic doublet refers to:
o: Two aftershocks of exactly equal magnitude from the same rupture
Two independent earthquakes of similar size
Two volcanic eruptions from adjacent craters
One earthquake followed by a tsunami
accepted.x: A seismic doublet consists of two independent earthquakes of similar size. Such an event was described near Caracas on the Caribbean–South American strike-slip boundary.
accepted.tq: Resolve the technical term by separating independent similar events from aftershocks or related hazards.

accepted.s: The Caracas seismic doublet occurred on which type of plate boundary?
accepted.x: The Caracas doublet occurred on the Caribbean–South American strike-slip boundary.
accepted.tq: Associate the event with its named boundary type and avoid substituting a generic plate-boundary category.

accepted.s: Which of the following recent earthquake-event pairs is correctly matched?
o: M 7.7 — off Flores Island, Indonesia — August 2026
accepted.x: An M 7.7 earthquake struck off Flores Island, Indonesia, on 18 August 2026. The other events have been paired with incorrect locations or magnitudes.
accepted.tq: Check magnitude, location and date together to defeat swapped-event distractors.

accepted.s: The M 8.8 megathrust earthquake off Kamchatka in August 2025 was notable because it:
o: Produced a tsunami that completely inundated the Pacific coast
Occurred on the Caracas strike-slip boundary
accepted.x: Despite its M 8.8 megathrust magnitude, the Kamchatka earthquake caused only a limited tsunami.
accepted.tq: Focus on the unusual consequence of the event rather than inferring impact solely from magnitude.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about seismicity in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Most of Andhra Pradesh lies in Seismic Zones II and III.
2. Reservoir-triggered tremors cannot be ruled out near Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam and Polavaram.
3. Old faults in the Eastern Ghats are relevant to the possibility of tremors.
4. Visakhapatnam lies in Zone V.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Visakhapatnam is in Zone II, not Zone V.
accepted.tq: Find the location-based false statement by checking the specific seismic zone assigned to Visakhapatnam.

accepted.s: An earthquake of magnitude 4.4, at a depth of 5 km, near Koraput–Jeypore shook which areas in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Araku and Paderu in ASR district
accepted.x: The M 4.4 earthquake near Koraput–Jeypore in Odisha, at a depth of 5 km, shook Araku and Paderu in the ASR district.
accepted.tq: Combine the magnitude, depth and affected-location clues to identify the event precisely.

accepted.s: The withdrawn earthquake hazard map was based on how many earthquake events and seismogenic zones?
accepted.x: The withdrawn map was based on 69,519 events and 36 seismogenic zones.
accepted.tq: Keep the two numerical components paired; the distractors reverse or alter one of the figures.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the change concerning Zone VI in IS 1893:2025?
o: Zone VI was notified and subsequently withdrawn on 3 March 2026.
Zone VI was notified permanently on 3 March 2026.
Zone VI was withdrawn before being notified in 2025.
Zone VI was notified only for Andhra Pradesh and retained without change.
accepted.x: Zone VI was notified in IS 1893:2025 and was subsequently withdrawn on 3 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Track the sequence of notification followed by withdrawal and reject reversed timelines.

accepted.s: Experts criticised the restored 2016 earthquake-hazard values mainly because they considered them:
o: Applicable only to coastal Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: Experts argued that the restored 2016 hazard values were too low for the Himalaya. NDMA, in contrast, described the new values as too high.
accepted.tq: Separate the contrasting positions of experts and NDMA instead of treating both criticisms as identical.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about earthquake safety and construction is correct?
o: Construction cost is irrelevant to the debate over PSHA-based codes.
Approximately 95% of earthquake deaths occur in poorly built one- to three-storey houses.
Retrofitting is unnecessary when a building follows no seismic code.
Earthquake deaths occur almost exclusively in high-rise steel buildings.
accepted.x: About 95% of earthquake deaths occur in poorly built one- to three-storey houses. The debate also involves balancing safer PSHA-based codes against construction costs.
accepted.tq: Apply the risk statistic to a built-environment scenario and reject exaggerated building claims.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the FIRST step among NDMA's six pillars of seismic safety?
o: Replacing all reservoirs with underground water tanks
Building according to IS 1893, IS 4326 and IS 13920, along with prioritising important buildings for retrofitting
Banning all construction in Seismic Zone II
accepted.x: The first pillar begins with construction according to IS 1893, IS 4326 and IS 13920, together with retrofitting priority buildings.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional safety measure that directly addresses structural vulnerability.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh and earthquake risk is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh lies entirely in Zone V and has no reservoir-related seismic risk.
The Eastern Ghats have no old faults relevant to seismicity.
Only coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh can experience earthquakes.
Although Andhra Pradesh lies mainly in Zones II and III, reservoir-triggered tremors remain possible near major reservoirs and along old Eastern Ghats faults.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is mainly in Zones II and III, but tremors associated with reservoirs and old Eastern Ghats faults cannot be ruled out.
accepted.tq: Combine the general regional classification with the important stated exception.
